core_obligations: Reduce to topology: the statement only uses the underlying topological spaces and the projection p: X_K to X (proof lines 1112-1113).
For t in T_K and C the connected component of X_K containing t, show p(C) is connected and meets T, hence p(C) is contained in the connected component T (proof lines 1114-1117).
Conclude C is contained in T_K, so T_K is a union of connected components of X_K (proof lines 1117-1118).
proof_roadmap: Note the statement is topological (proof lines 1112-1113).
Compare the connected component through a point of T_K with T through its image (proof lines 1114-1117).
Conclude the containment C in T_K (proof lines 1117-1118).
difficulty_reason: For an extension of fields K/k and a scheme X over k, the inverse image of a connected component of X under the projection X_K to X is a union of connected components of X_K (statement lines 1103-1109). The author observes that the assertion is purely topological and then argues directly: for a point t of T_K and the connected component C of X_K containing it, the image p(C) is connected and meets T, so p(C) lies in T and therefore C lies in T_K (proof lines 1112-1117). The claim is H2: a short topological argument, with the only step beyond formality being the use that the connected component T is closed under the connected image p(C) once that image meets T.
